Consistent with our most recent discussions and correspondence with our stockholders, EOG will provide the following disclosures as part of an update to our website disclosures in 2016:
•
EOG’s 2015 methane emissions intensity rate — this new quantitative measure will show EOG’s methane-specific fugitive emissions
associated with our operated wells for 2015 relative to our total company production of oil and gas for 2015, based on the greenhouse gas emissions EOG currently reports pursuant to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s greenhouse gas
reporting program;
•
an update regarding EOG’s design and implementation of a formal, voluntary leak detection and repair (“LDAR”) program — our LDAR
program will include the use of infrared cameras and other thermal imaging technology; and
•
an update regarding our efforts to minimize emissions at our facilities, including the installation of low-bleed controllers and no-bleed controllers.
We expect to provide these and other updates to our website disclosures by the end of the second quarter of
2016.
Codes of Conduct and Ethics and Corporate Governance Guidelines
Pursuant to NYSE and SEC rules, we have adopted a Code of Business Conduct and Ethics (“Code of Conduct”) that applies to all of
our directors, officers and employees, and a Code of Ethics for Senior Financial Officers (“Code of Ethics”) that applies to our principal executive officer, principal financial officer, principal accounting officer and controllers.
You can access our Code of Conduct and Code of Ethics on our website at www.eogresources.com/about/corpgov.html, and any
stockholder who so requests may obtain a copy of our Code of Conduct or Code of Ethics by submitting a written request to our Corporate Secretary. We intend to disclose any amendments to our Code of Conduct or Code of Ethics and any waivers with
respect to our Code of Conduct or Code of Ethics granted to our principal executive officer, our principal financial officer, our principal

sustainable cost reductions across all areas.
•
Added significant new net resource potential and more than 3,000 net drilling locations in the Delaware Basin and the Bakken play.
•
Maintained a strong balance sheet, ending the year with a net debt-to-total capitalization ratio* of 31%.
•
Continued to achieve outstanding performance from the Eagle Ford, Delaware Basin and Bakken.
Despite EOG’s outstanding operational achievements in 2015, the worldwide commodity price decline negatively impacted both
EOG’s financial results and stock price. Yet, while the price of oil declined 30.5% in 2015, our stock price only declined 23.1%, compared to an average decline of 41.4% among our peers. In light of the current commodity price environment, the
Committee took the following key actions in 2015:
•
Froze executive officer salaries, including the salaries of all of the Named Officers;
•
Reduced the grant date values of the 2015 long-term incentive awards by approximately 32% compared to 2014 grant values; and
•
Reduced 2015 bonus payments by approximately 22% compared to 2014 bonus payments.
Additionally, with a significant portion of our Named Officers’ total compensation tied to long-term incentives, the value of their
outstanding (i.e., unvested) holdings of EOG stock was reduced in 2015 relative to the 2014 value of such holdings, reflecting the decline in EOG’s stock price during 2015. The Committee believes these actions appropriately reflect the impact
of the current commodity price environment on our business and stock price, while continuing to appropriately reward our executive officers for EOG’s strong performance operationally and relative to peers.

Say-on-Pay Vote and Key Program Features
At our 2015 annual meeting of stockholders, the vast majority of our stockholders voted to approve our executive compensation program,
with nearly 97% approval among votes cast. Based on these voting results and the Committee’s periodic reviews of our executive compensation program, we did not make any significant changes to our executive compensation program for 2015. Our
program continues to reflect an alignment with current governance trends, while maintaining a competitive compensation program with stockholder-friendly features such as:
•
A structured annual bonus plan that is tied to annual operational, financial and strategic goals, including individual bonus targets and weightings for
each goal used to determine the bonuses, while preserving the Committee’s ability to qualitatively assess the performance of our Named Officers.
•
Significant alignment with our stockholders in the form of annual stock grants with long-service vesting requirements of five-year “cliff”
vesting for performance units and restricted stock/restricted stock units (“RSUs”) and four-year ratable vesting for stock-settled stock appreciation rights (“SARs”).
•
A performance-based long-term incentive plan (consisting of grants of performance units)

Stockholder Communications with the Board
Pursuant to the process adopted by the Board, our stockholders and other interested parties may communicate with members of the Board by submitting such communications in writing to our Corporate
Secretary, who, upon receipt of any communication other than one that is clearly marked “Confidential,” will note the date the communication was received in a log established for that purpose, open the communication, make a copy of it for
our files and promptly forward the communication to the director(s) to whom it is addressed. Upon receipt of any communication that is clearly marked “Confidential,” our Corporate Secretary will not open the communication, but will note
the date the communication was received in a log established for that purpose and promptly forward the communication to the director(s) to whom it is addressed. Further information regarding this process can be found on our website at
